method_as_stated: SIMULATION (performed by E. Ducrot): HOOMD-blue, cited as Anderson et al. 2008 and Glaser et al. 2015; version, integrator, thermostat, time step and cooling rate are NOT stated in the file. Each particle is four partially overlapping spheres in tetrahedral arrangement, and the attractive patches are modelled as the exposed surface of a sphere centred on the cluster's centre of mass. Two geometric parameters: compression ratio dcc/(2a), the lobe centre-to-centre distance over the lobe diameter, and size ratio b/a, the patch's radial extent over the lobe radius. Patch-patch attraction is a 2n-n Lennard-Jones form with n = 24 and well depth 10 (set arbitrarily), its minimum at 2^(1/n) sigma = 1.03 sigma with sigma the sphere radius; lobe-lobe attraction the same form with depth 3, standing for weak depletion by F-127 micelles and a little DNA; lobe-patch is a purely repulsive WCA-type form of the same exponent with strength 10. For these parameters the patch melting temperature is 1.6 to 1.7 in the model's energy units; a shorter-ranged n = 48 variant was also explored. A typical run holds 216 to 8,000 particles in a periodic box at 5% volume fraction, cooled slowly near the aggregation temperature; the final state is classified with OVITO as crystal or random aggregate. EXPERIMENT: four 1.0-um polystyrene spheres aggregated on a ~500-nm TPM oil droplet (tetrahedra with fewer than 1 in 1,000 not tetrahedral after density-gradient separation), compressed by THF, patches functionalised with self-complementary DNA; crystallised in a 50/50 D2O/PBS buffer (10 mM, pH 7.4, 280 mM NaCl, 1 wt% F-127) in a 100 um x 2 mm x 5 cm capillary tilted about 20 degrees, with a ~1 degC gradient spanning the DNA melting temperature of about 40 degC; imaged by bright field (Nikon Eclipse TiE), confocal (Leica SP8) and SEM. PHOTONIC BANDS by MIT Photonic Bands (223 k-vectors, 32^3 grid) and FDTD.
